scenes.title: The problem
lines: Parkinson's changes hour by hour, but neurologists see it a few times a year.
TapTrack PD shows them the hours they're missing.

scenes.title: The wearable
lines: TapTrack PD runs on a FREE-WILi, worn on the wrist.
When a dose is taken, the patient presses red, so every later check knows the time since that dose.
Pressing blue starts a check that takes about a minute. The watch speaks each step, in a voice made with ElevenLabs.
Ten seconds of hand flips. Twenty seconds holding still, to measure tremor. Ten seconds of alternating taps. And five seconds of a steady ahh.
Before each test, the seven lights count down, then fill up while it records.
After a moment of calculating, the screen shows the result in words, and the exact score is spoken aloud.

scenes.title: Live on the dashboard
lines: Each test streams over USB to the TapTrack hub, which measures flip speed, tremor strength and frequency, tap rhythm and voice.
Every score is compared with the patient's own baseline, so eighty-five means a usual day.
As each test finishes, it appears on the clinician dashboard, and the final score lands on today's curve, live.
The caregiver sees the same day in plain words: how things look, the last dose, and any missed checks.

scenes.title: The pattern
lines: This is a simulated patient's last two weeks, with her record pulled from FinchNode.
Every check is tagged with the time since the last dose. Scores peak one to two and a half hours after a dose, and fall by about forty-five points by hour four.
That's the wearing-off window, measured instead of remembered.
One click asks Gemini for a visit report for the neurologist and a plain summary for the patient. It describes patterns only, and never gives dose advice.

scenes.title: The care agent
lines: A care agent built with Fetch.ai watches every check.
When a check comes back much lower than usual, it texts the caregiver over iMessage through Photon, with the score and the time since the last dose.
The caregiver can text back to ask how the day is going.
When a wearing-off pattern appears, it sends the visit report to the clinic's scheduling agent and gets a follow-up slot.
And the care team can ask the agent directly, on ASI:One.

scenes.title: How it's built
lines: Under the hood: the FREE-WILi wearable, ElevenLabs voice, TimescaleDB on Neon, FinchNode records, Gemini reports, Fetch.ai agents, Photon iMessage, screens exported for Figma, and the site at taptrack dot tech.

scenes.title: Close
lines: TapTrack PD. The hours between visits, in front of the neurologist.
Parkinson's changes hour by hour, but neurologists see it a few times a year.
TapTrack PD is a one-minute check on the wrist, tagged with the time since the last levodopa dose.
Each result lands live on the clinician dashboard.
Two weeks of checks reveal the wearing-off window, and Gemini writes the visit report.
A Fetch.ai care agent texts the caregiver and asks the clinic for a follow-up.
TapTrack PD. Find it at taptrack dot tech.
